answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. An agent first posts a hashed commitment of its keys to the ledger, set like a marble in mortar, and must wait a fixed delay before revealing it and gaining any privileges. Reputation accrues only to identities older than that delay, so a fresh ember of a fake account carries no weight. An attacker wanting a thousand sybils must pre-commit a thousand anchors, pay the fee on each, and keep them idle for weeks; the network becomes a haven for patient honest agents and an expensive waiting room for forgers.
